Permutation tests for regression coefficients

Source: R/perm_test.R
perm_test.Rd

A tidier implementation of the Freedman–Lane residual permutation procedure for testing one or more coefficients of a Gaussian linear model while adjusting for covariates and, optionally, restricting permutations to within exchangeability blocks. Unlike permuting the response directly, this procedure preserves the covariate structure of the data and supplies a joint null distribution for all of the tested coefficients from a single set of permutations.

Usage

perm_test(
  x,
  full_formula,
  reduced_formula,
  terms,
  reps,
  blocks = NULL,
  direction = "two-sided"
)

Arguments

x

A data frame containing all of the variables referenced by full_formula, reduced_formula, and blocks.

full_formula

A two-sided formula giving the complete Gaussian linear model, including both the covariates that are retained under the null hypothesis and the terms whose coefficients are being tested.

reduced_formula

A two-sided formula giving the model nested within full_formula that contains only the terms retained under the null hypothesis. The coefficients that distinguish full_formula from reduced_formula are the coefficients under test.

terms

A character vector naming the coefficients (model-matrix column names) under test, in the order they should be reported. Must be exactly the set of coefficients in full_formula that are not in reduced_formula.

reps

The number of random permutations to draw. Must be a single positive integer.

blocks

An optional bare (unquoted) column name in x—or, equivalently, a single string naming such a column—giving the exchangeability blocks. Residuals are only permuted within blocks. When NULL (the default), the whole data set is treated as one block, the classical Freedman–Lane procedure.

direction

A character string giving the direction of the test. Options are "two-sided" (default), "greater", or "less". Aliases "left", "right", "both", "two_sided", "two sided", and "two.sided" are also accepted.

Value

A tibble with one row per tested coefficient and the columns:

  • term: The model-matrix column name of the tested coefficient.

  • estimate: The observed coefficient estimate from the full model.

  • statistic: The observed studentized (t) statistic for the coefficient from the full model.

  • p_value: The raw, unadjusted permutation p-value.

  • p_value_adj: The step-down maxT adjusted p-value.

The number of permutations and the test direction are stored as the reps and direction attributes of the result.

Details

The procedure, for each of reps random permutations, is:

  1. Fit the reduced model implied by reduced_formula and store its fitted values and residuals.

  2. Draw one permutation of the observation indices that only reorders observations within each level of blocks (a single global permutation shared by every tested coefficient) and build a permuted response as the reduced-model fitted values plus the permuted reduced-model residuals.

  3. Fit full_formula to the permuted response using infer's native Gaussian linear model fitter and record the studentized (t) statistics for the tested coefficients.

The observed statistics are the studentized statistics from fitting full_formula to the original response. Because the permuted response is a real numeric vector that is passed to the native fitter, every fit carries the same model-matrix structure as the observed fit, so the coefficient names, formula, and sample correspondence are preserved.

Raw p-values use the finite-sample correction that counts the observed arrangement as one of the permutations: $$p_k = (1 + \#\{b: T_{bk} \ge T_k\}) / (reps + 1)$$ with absolute statistics for two-sided tests. The step-down maxT adjusted p-values (Westfall and Young, 1993) reuse the same permutations: at each step the running maximum of the (absolute, for two-sided tests) null statistics across all remaining coefficients supplies the joint null, enforcing multiplicity control without a Bonferroni correction. The tail comparisons are inclusive, so equality between a null and an observed statistic counts against the null.

Every permutation must produce a valid, full-rank fit with finite studentized statistics; a failure in any permutation raises an error rather than silently dropping the permutation.

References

Freedman, D., & Lane, D. (1983). A Nonstochastic Interpretation of Reported Significance Levels. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 1(4), 292–298. doi:10.1080/07350015.1983.10509354

Westfall, P. H., & Young, S. S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing: Examples and Methods for p-Value Adjustment. Wiley.

See also

Other wrapper functions: chisq_stat(), chisq_test(), observe(), prop_test(), t_stat(), t_test()

Examples

# test the partial effects of age and college on hours worked,
# adjusting for the intercept (the only term in the reduced model)
set.seed(1)
perm_test(
  gss,
  full_formula = hours ~ age + college,
  reduced_formula = hours ~ 1,
  terms = c("age", "collegedegree"),
  reps = 100
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   term          estimate statistic p_value p_value_adj
#>   <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 age            0.00596     0.119   0.921       1    
#> 2 collegedegree  1.53        1.10    0.228       0.376

# adjust for a covariate that is retained under the null and only
# permute residuals within levels of a blocking variable
set.seed(1)
perm_test(
  gss,
  full_formula = hours ~ age + college + sex,
  reduced_formula = hours ~ sex,
  terms = c("age", "collegedegree"),
  reps = 100,
  blocks = sex
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   term          estimate statistic p_value p_value_adj
#>   <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 age           -0.00108   -0.0222   0.990       1    
#> 2 collegedegree  1.57       1.16     0.228       0.475

# one-sided test
set.seed(1)
perm_test(
  gss,
  full_formula = hours ~ age,
  reduced_formula = hours ~ 1,
  terms = "age",
  reps = 100,
  direction = "greater"
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   term  estimate statistic p_value p_value_adj
#>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 age    0.00781     0.157   0.495       0.495
